audit.whatIsWrong: Apprehend is correctly identified as the ability that decides the lane and is referenced in nine fields, but its cooldown is never given once — 'His all-in start', 'on Apprehend's cooldown', 'on its long cooldown'.
audit.why: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1, falling to 16s at rank 5. It is by a wide margin the longest cooldown either champion has in lane, and against Ambessa's 13s Lacerate that means she gets two full trade attempts inside one missed pull. 'Long cooldown' is not a plan; 26 seconds is.
audit.corrected: tldr, winCon, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t now carry the 26s and 16s numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Apprehend is treated purely as a pull. Its passive half — the reason armour underperforms in this matchup — is absent from both layers, while report[8] recommends Plated Steelcaps without qualification.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Darius hones his axe, passively causing his physical damage to ignore a percentage of his target's Armor.' Every point of armour Ambessa buys is discounted before Decimate and Crippling Strike land, and Noxian Guillotine is true damage on top, so armour is a partial answer here rather than the answer.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and report[8].t now state that his E passive shreds part of your armour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was the generic 'the R lock isolates and finishes the chain — point it at the kill, not the tank'. Noxian Guillotine's cost curve was never mentioned.
audit.why: Noxian Guillotine is 120s at rank 1 but costs 100 mana at ranks 1 and 2 and nothing at rank 3, and it deals true damage with the cooldown refreshed on a kill. Public Execution at 130s is a slower ultimate than his — the flip only works because the suppress lands before Apprehend can grip, not because Ambessa out-cooldowns him.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names both ultimates and states that armour does not answer Guillotine.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2's 'why' claimed 'dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade', and Levels 4-5 said 'the lane-control window: trade around Apprehend's cooldown and bank small leads' while the content layer calls the same stage Ambessa's weakest window.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund — no shield; Repudiation is her only shield. At 4-5 Apprehend is already down to 18.5s while her own Q and E are at their longest, so the two layers were describing opposite lanes.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why and phases[3].why now match the content layer and carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Crippling Strike is described as a slow and a source of bleed. That it is an attack reset is stated nowhere, so the page never tells you what the actual burst tell looks like.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Darius's next attack strikes an enemy's crucial artery' — it is an on-next-attack reset on a flat 5s cooldown. The moment to step out is the attack wind-up, not the ability cast, and at 5s he can hold it through most of Ambessa's short trades.
audit.corrected: whys[0], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t now name the reset and the 5s cooldown.

edits.after: Bait Apprehend: 26s at rank 1 is your window. Weave the combo and never bleed to five.

edits.before: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Eclipse  (burst + the dash tempo), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Anti-heal (Oblivion Orb / Executioner's) early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Eclipse (burst + the dash tempo), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps, though Apprehend's passive shreds part of it. Oblivion Orb early — Decimate heals him.

edits.before: Darius out-trades you at 1: a Crippling Strike (W) auto and instant Hemorrhage bleed beat your single energy-gated ability before any combo exists.
edits.after: Darius out-trades you at 1: Crippling Strike is a 5s attack reset, so the wind-up is the hit, and Hemorrhage bleeds before your combo exists.

notes: Ambessa's kit file flags grounding on Repudiation and grounding plus heal on Public Execution; Riot's descriptions of both abilities contain none of that, so I never claimed W or R grounds Darius or heals her — which matters because the content layer already leans on an 'R passive heal' in three places. I left those strings alone rather than delete a claim I cannot settle from the data, but it is not in Riot's Public Execution text and the user should check it. Darius's kit file flags knockup on Apprehend; Riot's text says he 'sweeps up his enemies with his axe's hook and pulls them to him', so I wrote it as a pull throughout. Noxian Guillotine's mana cost curve is 100/100/0, which is why it is free from rank 3.
